concept: MTPLX Forge and MTP-preserving MLX conversion
summary: 2.9.2 (25 Aug 2026): Forge correctness fix for the MTP norm convention.

facts.text: 2.9.2 (25 Aug 2026): Forge correctness fix for the MTP norm convention.
2.12.0 (Sep 2026): Forge converts Flash-Next source models (issue 508).
The home page describes the flow as "paste a Hugging Face link".
A wrong norm convention collapsed draft acceptance to 0-2% on some packs until 2.9.2.
A trunk shifted twice (norm offset applied twice) is now refused by the runtime with a clear error.
A Forge verdict can be that MTP does not help: the tool reports "Depth 1 is fastest" style results from measurement rather than assuming a gain.
None found. All Forge claims are first-party (MTPLX README and release notes); no third party describes using Forge.
What data and how many steps Forge uses to train the MTP adapter is not in the cached pages.
Whether Forge can preserve an existing in-checkpoint MTP head losslessly, as against training a new adapter, is not stated.
Third-party reproduction of Forge speedups is missing.

MTPLX Forge turns a Hugging Face repo into an MTPLX-ready MTP model by converting to MLX, training the MTP adapter, verifying the result is faster and still exact, and optionally publishing to the Hub.
`mtplx forge --help` lists probe, build, publish and verify subcommands, and Forge is also a screen in the Mac app.
Pulls and Forge builds always write to the primary model root; extra `model_dirs` are discovery-only, and CLI updates or removals in an extra root need `--cache-dir` naming that root.
MTPLX 2.9.2 (25 Aug 2026) decides the MTP norm convention once per tensor set, which rescued packs whose draft acceptance had collapsed to 0-2%.
Since 2.9.2 the MTPLX runtime refuses a double-shifted trunk with a clear error instead of running it.
MTPLX 2.12.0 lets Forge convert Flash-Next source models (issue 508, contributed by bpmforge).
The MTPLX home page describes Forge as "paste a Hugging Face link; Forge converts it to MLX and measures the speedup on your Mac."
The official Youssofal catalog includes FP16 builds of Qwen 3.8 27B for M1 and M2, a Qwen 3.6 35B MoE balance build, and Gemma 4 packs.
A merge commit in the MTPLX repo lists `mtplx/commands/forge.py`, `compressed_tensors.py`, `gdn_capture.py` and `mtp_patch.py` as the conflicting modules of the 2.9.2 staging merge.
The MTPLX repo's CI fails any push whose history contains AI authorship or co-author attribution.
